summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic left-sided chest pain, diastolic heart failure, recurrent pulmonary embolism on anticoagulation, and prior gastrointestinal bleeding presented with an exacerbation of her typical burning chest pain, which worsened with deep breathing and was associated with left arm and jaw discomfort. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, and aortic pathology via normal EKG, serial cardiac enzymes, and a negative CTA. The pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, consistent with costochondritis, and not cardiac in origin. She was found to have acute on chronic iron deficiency anemia with trace guaiac-positive stools, likely due to chronic gastritis exacerbated by intermittent NSAID use and long-term anticoagulation. Despite the bleeding risk, warfarin was continued due to high thrombotic risk, while omeprazole was uptitrated to 40 mg twice daily and iron supplementation was initiated. NSAIDs were discontinued, and she was referred to gastroenterology for outpatient endoscopic evaluation. Her heart failure and hypertension remained stable, managed on home medications. She was discharged home with improved pain control and stable hemoglobin, on a revised medication regimen emphasizing GI protection and safe analgesia with acetaminophen.
problems: Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Nonspecific abnormal findings in stool contents
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Atrophic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
